summary: @onereach/bandwidth-steps-voice-bxml ships obfuscated preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime to execute bundled payload
details: The package's preinstall lifecycle runs setup.mjs, an obfuscated script (hex-mangled identifiers, proxy-object dispatch tables) that detects the host platform (including ldd/musl/Alpine handling), downloads the Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/, extracts the bun binary to a tmpdir, chmods it 0o755, and execFileSync's it against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727KB @bun-cjs blob using classic string-array rotation obfuscation (WV8StW rotator, opaque n7gIxM constant array, hex identifiers). The filename math_init has no relationship to the package's advertised purpose (Bandwidth Voice BXML step wrappers), and the payload is delivered outside Node's loader specifically so it runs under an alien runtime fetched at install. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: an installer running `npm install` automatically fetches a foreign runtime and executes an obfuscated bundle whose contents are not inspectable through normal Node tooling. Both the preinstall dropper and the payload it executes are obfuscated, and the payload's purpose does not correspond to any documented functionality of the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
